proof:
# Exact weighted Doignon extremality with arbitrarily many positive fibers

For any n>=1 and integer L>=1, put

Z_L={0,1}^{n-1} x {1,...,2L}

and give these points equal positive weights. Its maximal normalized ambient halfspace depth is exactly2^{-n}, independently of L.

To prove the lower bound, fix any binary vertex v in {0,1}^{n-1} and choose j=L or L+1. Every closed halfspace containing (v,j), restricted to the line {v} x R, contains at least L of that line's2L integer points. The total number of points is2^{n-1}(2L), so the depth is at least2^{-n}.

For the upper bound, take any candidate (v,j). A one-dimensional closed tail containing j contains at most L of the2L integer points if j is a median, and at most L for every other j by choosing its smaller tail. Let its defining inequality be a t>=b, with a either1 or-1. Define

F_v(z)=sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(2v_i-1)z_i.

It is uniquely maximized at v among binary vertices, with gap at least one to every other vertex. For sufficiently large M, the ambient halfspace

a t+M(F_v(z)-F_v(v))>=b

agrees with the chosen tail on the v-line and excludes every other binary line. It contains at most L points, proving the upper bound. For n=1 the binary factor and exposing term are omitted; this is the ordinary exact median bound on2L equally weighted points.

These positive weights are realized by genuine full-dimensional mixed fibers: take any d-dimensional convex body K of positive volume and

C_L=[0,1]^{n-1} x [1,2L] x K.

Every integer fiber is a copy of K. The weighted integer marginal is exactly the uniform measure above. For L>1, each fiber has normalized weight1/[2^{n-1}(2L)]<2^{-n}, so the example lies in the non-heavy regime.

Nevertheless the number of positive fibers is2^n L, and the remaining integer interval has length2L-1. These quantities are unbounded while marginal depth is exactly at the Doignon constant. Consequently near-extremality of weighted integer-marginal depth cannot by itself force bounded support, bounded remaining lattice width, or a finite list of bounded lattice configurations.

The same phenomenon allows unequal positive weights. In one integer dimension, any positive weight sequence symmetric about the half-integer L+1/2 has equal mass in its left and right halves and maximal weighted halfspace depth exactly1/2. Concave positive scaling profiles symmetric about that half-integer realize many such sequences as convex-body fiber volumes. Adding the n-1 binary coordinates preserves the exact factor2^{-(n-1)} by the same exposing argument.

This is not a counterexample to OC. It shows that sharpness or near-sharpness of the integer marginal is too weak, by itself, to force the finite extremal geometry sought by that proof route.
